name: steps
description:
The progress rail a `step` sits on. Three or four thin bars across the top of a multi-stage form, filled up to where you are.

It exists because deleting it was a mistake. `steps` was in the superseded `components` map and went with it, on the assumption that every class in that map had an actor replacement. `step` did — it is a leaf, and it was promoted. `steps` did not: it was the flex parent the leaf's `flex: 1` needs, and without it every rail in the estate collapsed to nothing while the gates stayed green, because a missing container is not a broken class.

So the pair is a pair again: `steps` is the rail, `step` is one stage on it, and neither is any use alone.

base.$description:
A flex row so each `step` can take an equal share through its own `flex: 1`, and full width because the rail measures the whole form rather than its own contents. That second half is what was missing: dropped into a card that centres its children, a content-sized rail is a rail of zero bars.

`aria-hidden` in the view, not by accident. The rail is decorative — the stage a reader needs is said in words beside it ('Schritt 2 von 3'), because a filled bar is colour-only information.

a11y.note: Decorative and marked so. A progress rail conveys position by fill alone, which is colour-only information; the surfaces that use it state the stage in text beside it, and that text is what a screen reader gets.
